In mathematical group theory, a [[subgroup]] of a [[Group (mathematics)|group]] is termed a '''special abelian subgroup''' or '''SA-subgroup''' if the centralizer of any nonidentity element in the subgroup is precisely the subgroup{{harv|Curtis|Reiner|1981|loc=p.354}}. Equivalently, an SA subgroup is a [[centrally closed subgroup|centrally closed]] [[Abelian group|abelian]] subgroup. 

* Any SA subgroup is a maximal abelian subgroup, that is, it is not properly contained in another abelian subgroup.
* For a [[CA group]], the SA subgroups are precisely the maximal abelian subgroups.

SA subgroups are known for certain characters associated with them termed [[exceptional character]]s.
